This afternoon, clear rules for water bowls
Staff will learn the main rule first, then the reasons

Companion Animal Travel Desk Water Bowl Handling
Purpose: This section sets the daily standard for safe water bowl handling so companion animals travel with steady care and the customer handoff stays calm.

At the desk, staff should check each bowl for clean condition, secure fit, and proper label match before any animal is accepted for service. Bowls must be emptied, rinsed, and refilled with fresh water when the carrier is prepared, and staff should keep the bowl upright during movement through the terminal. If a traveler asks for help, the team should give clear guidance in plain words and confirm the bowl is attached correctly before the animal leaves the desk area. <<FACT F087>> Staff should not improvise with loose containers, shared dishes, or bowls that do not belong to the same booking, because mixed equipment can cause confusion and delay.

When an animal is waiting for transfer, the bowl should remain with the carrier unless the senior coordinator directs a temporary removal for safety or cleaning. Any spill must be handled at once with a dry cloth or approved wipe, and the carrier should be checked again before it moves onward. If a traveler arrives with a special container, staff should inspect it for stability and cleanliness, then decide whether it can be used without creating a hazard. The Companion Animal Travel Desk should keep a calm tone throughout, since a steady hand helps the animal settle and helps the traveler trust the process. For example, if Rafael Clark or Sofia Haddad arrives with Cali, staff should keep the same handling standard and speak gently while they work.

If a bowl is damaged, missing, or difficult to secure, the desk must pause the handoff and arrange a substitute before the animal proceeds. Staff should record any exception in the booking notes and pass the case to the next shift without delay. Questions about unusual equipment, animal comfort, or follow-up care should go to the senior coordinator or the duty supervisor, who will guide the next step.
